messages:
Jordan: FYI nightly e2e perf gate tripped on p95 + throughput this morning. p95 +28% vs baseline, throughput -12%. Screenshot: https://redwood.internal/ci/2501234567/logs
Dev-Bot: nightly-e2e-run #7823 -> FAILED (perf-gate). Check /ci/nightly/7823
Priya: which suite failed? longseq or mixedseq?
Jordan: longseq-heavy. Failing metric appears in the longseq p95 bucket. Full job link above.
Sam: can run a quick rerun on the same commit to rule out flake. Want me to kick it?
Jordan: please do. Also if rerun fails, let's request a bisect across the last green -> current. Suspect range is 0f3a2b1..a7c9d4f (approx).
Li: longseq is noisy; long-window p95 can be sensitive to infra noise. If rerun passes, we should run an isolated throughput sweep (no batching changes) to confirm.
Sam: rerun queued: /ci/retry 7823 -> started. cluster: infra-us-west-2-nightly, runner: e2e-03
Dev-Bot: Retry #1 for nightly-e2e-run 7823 started by Sam at 2026-03-17T09:12:34Z
Sam: quick note — I'll disable the kvcache warmup step in the rerun to isolate cache noise (flag: --no-kvcache-warm).
Priya: good plan. If rerun still shows p95 delta, can we bisect only the model-onboarding commits first (they changed compilation kernels last week)?
Jordan: yes, model-onboard subset is commits a7c9000..a7c9d4f (small set). If rerun fails, start bisection there first.
Dev-Bot: Retry #1 completed -> PASSED. Metrics: p95 delta +6%, throughput -3% (within tolerated drift but gate rules still mark red). Details: /ci/nightly/7823/retry/1/metrics
Li: interesting — rerun passed but still higher p95 than baseline. That points to baseline shift rather than transient. Need to run a controlled perf harness with 5000 requests and pinned seeds.
Sam: I'll schedule a perf-harness job against the same commit + baseline commit. Perf-harness id: ph-449.
Priya: I'll own the bisect if perf-harness reproduces. Can someone collect the telemetry traces (token-level latency histograms + kernel selection logs) and upload to s3://redwood.perf/2501234567/?put
Jordan: uploaded logs and kernel profile tarball to s3://redwood.perf/2501234567/profiles.tar.gz
Dev-Bot: perf-harness ph-449 queued -> using infra-us-west-2-perf. Expected runtime ~45m
Sam: perf-harness complete -> ph-449: reproduced p95 +25% on longseq under controlled load. Trace: s3://redwood.perf/2501234567/ph-449/trace.json
Priya: ok bisect time. I'll start a targeted git-bisect over model-onboard commits tomorrow AM, focus on kernel selection changes and the compile-time flags. Will update this thread with progress.
Jordan: thanks Priya. If anyone's on-call overnight, ping me or @oncall. Priorities: 1) repro + traces (done) 2) bisect model-onboard subset (Priya) 3) if bisect points to kernel change, revert or tweak compile flags and run perf-harness.
Sam: noted. Leaving a bookmark: small local repro script to run: ./tools/perf/run_longseq.sh --seed 42 --iters 5000 --no-kvcache-warm
Li: also adding a note — check nvml/GPU power capping differences between baseline and current infra nodes; we saw similar drift last quarter from node firmware mismatch.
Priya: starting bisect now, will post candidates and timings. +1 to checking firmware.
Jordan: :thumbsup: thanks all. I'll open a quick tracking ticket in JIRA and link here once created.
Priya: created RED-4521 with triage notes and links to perf traces. Adding Sam and Li as watchers.
Sam: if you hit slow bisection, we can try partitioned bisection (split model-onboard subset in half) to accelerate.
Li: audible — happy to help analyze kernel profiles when we get bisect result.
Jordan: thread pinned for followups. Keep short updates here, ping if you need more CPU cycles on perf cluster.
